newsitem.title: UK: British MP in pyrrhic EU referendum victory.
newsitem.headline: British MP in pyrrhic EU referendum victory.

text.p: A Conservative anti-European member of parliament won a pyrrhic victory on Tuesday when she was given leave to introduce a bill for a nationwide referendum on whether Britain should remain a member of the European Union.
Teresa Gorman had hoped that a parliamentary vote on her move would reveal the depth of discontent with Brussels both in her own party and among opposition legislators.
But because of clever manoeuvring by her opponents, no vote ever took place.
This was a relief for Conservative Party managers who feared that her move could only expose once again the divisions in the party over Europe.
Gorman sought leave to bring in the bill under a procedure which allows MPs to test feeling among their colleagues on key issues, but which never enables them to pass legislation.

She told the lower House of Commons that EU red tape was frustrating, and sometimes killing, small businesses in her eastern England constituency, but ordinary people had no means of showing their disapproval.
"My constituents bitterly resent this, but they feel impotent to do anything about it," she said.
The vote did not take place because Gorman's foes deliberately refused to provide "tellers" to count members wishing to register their opposition to her proposed bill.

Gorman is one of eight Conservative MPs who were temporarily expelled from the parliamentary party two years ago for their refusal to obey the party line on Europe. She is a leading opponent of British membership of a single European currency.
A referendum in Britain in 1975 approved EU membership by a margin of two to one.

However, billionaire businessman Sir James Goldsmith has set up his own Referendum Party in Britain to press for a new plebiscite similar to that proposed by Gorman in the election which must be held in the next four months.
